coiffe.name: Rotator cuff tendinopathy
coiffe.whatYouFeel: Pain on the side of the shoulder and upper arm when lifting the arm, putting on a jacket, or at night when lying on it.
coiffe.whatHappens: Four tendons cap the head of the humerus and keep it centred as the arm rises. The supraspinatus tendon, at the top, is the one most often involved.
coiffe.whoIsAffected: Over 35, work or sport with the arms overhead.
coiffe.warning: After a fall, if you can no longer lift the arm: see a doctor promptly. Emergency (112 or your local number) if pain in the left shoulder or arm comes with chest tightness, shortness of breath or sweating, or appears on exertion. Hot, swollen shoulder with fever: see a doctor the same day.

conflit.name: Subacromial pain and bursitis
conflit.commonName: Shoulder that hurts when lifting the arm
conflit.whatYouFeel: Pain in an arc as the arm passes between 60 and 120°, eased with the arm by the side.
conflit.whatHappens: Under the acromion, a bursa separates the rotator cuff tendons from the bone. Tendons and bursa become sensitive when the load exceeds what they tolerate. The bone does not pinch the tendon: surgery that shaves it does no better than well-conducted rehabilitation.
conflit.whoIsAffected: Adults aged 30 to 60, repeated overhead movements.
conflit.warning: Severe night pain that comes on suddenly: see a doctor.

capsulite.name: Adhesive capsulitis
capsulite.whatYouFeel: Shoulder pain that is severe at first, especially at night, then a shoulder that becomes stiffer and stiffer in every direction.
capsulite.whatHappens: The joint capsule thickens and shrinks. It often lasts one to two years, in three stages: pain, stiffness, recovery.
capsulite.whoIsAffected: Between 40 and 60, more often women, more common with diabetes.
capsulite.warning: In the very painful phase, stay below the pain threshold: forcing makes it worse. Medical advice helps relieve this phase.

omarthrose.name: Glenohumeral osteoarthritis
omarthrose.whatYouFeel: Deep pain, stiffness especially when turning the arm outwards, cracking.
omarthrose.whatHappens: The cartilage between the head of the humerus and the glenoid thins and the bone remodels.
omarthrose.whoIsAffected: Over 60, after a fracture or an old rotator cuff tear.
omarthrose.warning: Night pain that does not respond to painkillers: see a doctor.

ac.name: Acromioclavicular joint pain
ac.commonName: Pain on top of the shoulder
ac.whatYouFeel: Pinpoint pain at the end of the collarbone, when crossing the arm in front of you or lying on that side.
ac.whatHappens: The small joint between the collarbone and the acromion wears, or keeps the after-effects of a sprain.
ac.whoIsAffected: Over 40 through wear, or after a fall on the shoulder, weightlifters.
ac.warning: After a fall, a visible step at the end of the collarbone: see a doctor.

calc.name: Calcific tendinopathy
calc.whatYouFeel: Moderate long-standing pain, then sometimes a very violent attack lasting a few days, with the shoulder locked by pain.
calc.whatHappens: A calcium deposit forms in a rotator cuff tendon. The attack corresponds to its reabsorption, after which the pain often goes away.
calc.warning: Very painful attack: see a doctor for pain relief.

rupture.name: Rotator cuff tear
rupture.whatYouFeel: Weakness when lifting the arm or holding it out to the side, night pain, sometimes little pain but an arm that no longer goes up.
rupture.whatHappens: The supraspinatus tendon comes away from the humerus, partly or completely. Neighbouring muscles can compensate after rehabilitation.
rupture.whoIsAffected: Over 60 through wear, or younger after a fall.
rupture.warning: Sudden loss of strength after a fall: see a doctor without delay, early repair is sometimes offered.

biceps.name: Long head of biceps tendinopathy
biceps.commonName: Pain at the front of the shoulder
biceps.whatYouFeel: Pinpoint pain at the front of the shoulder, in the groove of the humerus, when carrying something with the arm straight in front of you.
biceps.whatHappens: The long head of biceps tendon leaves the joint and slides in a groove at the front of the humerus, where it becomes irritated.
biceps.whoIsAffected: Throwing sports, swimming, carrying loads, often together with a rotator cuff problem.
biceps.warning: A snap followed by a lump appearing in the arm: see a doctor, the tendon may have ruptured.

instab.name: Shoulder instability
instab.whatYouFeel: Shoulder that comes out or feels about to come out with the arm raised and turned back, apprehension in that position.
instab.whatHappens: After a dislocation, the labrum and the ligaments at the front of the joint stay stretched and hold the head of the humerus less well.
instab.whoIsAffected: Young athletes after a first dislocation, contact and throwing sports.
instab.warning: A dislocated shoulder that does not go back: emergency (112 or your local number), do not try to put it back yourself. After a first dislocation, get examined: under 25 the risk of it happening again is high; over 40 a rotator cuff tendon is often torn. Numbness of the upper arm or weakness: see a doctor promptly.

slap.name: SLAP tear of the superior labrum
slap.whatYouFeel: Deep pain with the arm cocked back, sometimes catching or a loss of throwing speed.
slap.whatHappens: The labrum comes away at the top of the glenoid, where the long head of biceps tendon attaches.
slap.whoIsAffected: Throwing and racket sports, or after a fall on an outstretched arm.
slap.warning: Catching or pain that persists despite rehabilitation: see a doctor.

dysk.name: Scapular dyskinesis
dysk.whatYouFeel: Tiredness and pain around the shoulder blade, which lifts away from the chest wall as the arm comes down.
dysk.whatHappens: The serratus anterior and the lower trapezius hold the shoulder blade flat and steer it. When they work poorly, the shoulder loses its base.
dysk.whoIsAffected: Overhead athletes, long hours at a screen, after shoulder pain.
dysk.warning: A shoulder blade that suddenly sticks out a lot: see a doctor, a nerve may be involved.

subscap.name: Subscapularis tendinopathy
subscap.commonName: Pain at the front of the shoulder when rotating
subscap.whatYouFeel: Pain at the front of the shoulder when pulling the hand towards the belly against resistance or reaching behind the back.
subscap.whatHappens: The subscapularis, at the front of the shoulder blade, turns the arm inwards. Its tendon attaches to the small bump at the front of the humerus.
subscap.warning: Sudden weakness after an injury with the arm out to the side: see a doctor.

re.name: External rotation, elbow at the side
re.how: Press the back of the hand against a wall without moving. Hold 30 s, 5 times, then with a resistance band, 3 sets of 12.
re.videoSearch: shoulder external rotation isometric band rotator cuff

scap.name: Raise in the plane of the shoulder blade
scap.how: Arm straight, 30° forward, thumb up, raise to shoulder height. 3 sets of 10.

wall.name: Wall slide
wall.how: Forearms against the wall, slide them upwards. 2 sets of 10.
wall.videoSearch: wall slide shoulder exercise serratus anterior

pend.name: Pendulum
pend.how: Leaning forward, arm relaxed, small circles. 1 to 2 minutes, several times a day.

aide.name: Raise helped by the other arm
aide.how: Lying down, the good arm lifts the painful arm. 10 times, without forcing.

baton.name: External rotation with a stick
baton.how: Elbow at the side, the stick pushes the hand outwards. Hold 5 s, 10 times.

row.name: Band row
row.how: Elbows by your sides, pull while squeezing the shoulder blades. 3 sets of 12.

ri.name: Internal rotation with a band
ri.how: Elbow at the side, bring the hand towards the belly. 3 sets of 12.

flexb.name: Elbow curl, light weight
flexb.how: Palm up, lift in 2 s, lower in 4 s. 3 sets of 10.
flexb.videoSearch: eccentric biceps curl long head biceps tendinopathy rehab

etpec.name: Chest stretch
etpec.how: Forearm on a door frame, turn the trunk away. 3 times 30 s.

pushplus.name: Wall push-up plus
pushplus.how: Arms straight, spread the shoulder blades by pushing into the wall. 3 sets of 12.
pushplus.videoSearch: wall push up plus serratus anterior scapular dyskinesis

yw.name: Y and W lying face down
yw.how: Arms in a Y then a W, shoulder blades drawn down and together. 2 sets of 10.
yw.videoSearch: prone Y W exercise lower trapezius

iso.name: Holds, arm by the side
iso.how: Press the hand against a wall forwards, sideways, backwards. Hold 10 s, 5 times in each direction.
iso.videoSearch: isometric shoulder exercises elbow at side rehab

croise.name: Cross-body stretch
croise.how: Bring the arm across the chest with the other hand. 3 times 30 s.

aqua.name: Movement in water
aqua.how: In a pool, arms supported by the water, large slow circles. 10 to 15 minutes.
